title: Inner enumeration counting invariant
statement: Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, write $R(u,v)$ for the assertion that the type-$3$ query encoding $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ returns true, and write $I(u)$ for the assertion that the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$ returns true. Define $\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)$ to mean that some $u<\sigma.K$ with $I(u)$ reaches $t$ in at most $\sigma.i$ steps of $R$. Let $\operatorname{GS}(A,B_0,C;r,t,c)$ be the recursive predicate that at depth zero requires $C(c)$, and at each positive depth either requires $A(t)$ and recurses with $t+1,c+1$, or requires $B_0(t)$ and recurses with $t+1,c$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.u\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.cnt\le\sigma.u$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=0$. If, whenever $\operatorname{GS}$ holds at depth $\sigma.K-\sigma.u$, position $\sigma.u$, count $\sigma.cnt$, with first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)\land t\ne\sigma.v\land\neg R(t,\sigma.v)$, second predicate always true, and terminal condition $c=\sigma.cp$, the machine at state $\mathrm{vn}$ with $u=cnt=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine at state $\mathrm{uh}$ with registers $\sigma$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when that recursive condition holds together with $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: $\mathcal O$ is an oracle on four query types and binary words
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For all configurations satisfying the stated recursive condition, the $\mathrm{vn}$ machine with $u=cnt=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle,
let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$ be a register state with every register at
most $B$. Write $R(u,v)$ for the truth of the oracle's type-$3$ query on
$(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ and $I(u)$ for the truth of its type-$1$ query on $(x,u,\sigma.s)$.
Let $\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)$ mean that some $I$-code below $\sigma.K$ reaches $t$ in at
most $\sigma.i$ steps of $R$, and define $\operatorname{GS}(A,B_0,C;r,t,c)$ recursively
by $C(c)$ when $r=0$, and, when $r>0$, by either $A(t)$ and
$\operatorname{GS}(A,B_0,C;r-1,t+1,c+1)$, or $B_0(t)$ and
$\operatorname{GS}(A,B_0,C;r-1,t+1,c)$. Suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$,
$\sigma.u\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.cnt\le\sigma.u$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=0$.
If the stated $\operatorname{GS}$ condition with $r=\sigma.K-\sigma.u$, start
$t=\sigma.u$, count $c=\sigma.cnt$, first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)\land
t\ne\sigma.v\land\neg R(t,\sigma.v)$, second predicate always true, and terminal
condition $c=\sigma.cp$ implies that the machine initialized at the next-outer-vertex
stage with $u=cnt=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$
holds, then the machine initialized at the inner-enumeration test with state $\sigma$
terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when the same recursive condition holds
with terminal condition $c=\sigma.cp$ and $Q$.
